opportunities.title: [Bounty: $100] URL-encode path parameters in client `get`/`update` methods
opportunities.summary: ## Context `AgentClient.get(agentId)` and `update` build `path: /v1/agents/${agentId}` (`src/clients/agent-client.ts`, lines 22-24 and 37-40); `WalletClient.get` does the same with `${walletId}` (`src/clients/wallet-client.ts`, lines 18-22); `PaymentClient.get` with `${paymentId}` (`src/clients/payment-client.ts`, lines 27-31). The transport builds the URL with `new URL(cleanPath, baseUrl)` (`src/http/fetch-http-client.ts`, line 106) but never percent-encodes the interpolated segment. Any id containing `/`, `?`, `#`, or a space silently corrupts the request URL and can hit the wrong route. ## Proposed Change Add a small `encodePathSegment`/`encodeURIComponent` step in `BaseClient.request` (or in `buildUrl`) so interpolated path parameters are always percent-encoded before the URL is constructed. ## Acceptance Criteria - A `get` call with an id containing `/` or `?` hits the correctly encoded path - `BaseClient` is the single place that handles path encoding for all clients - Encoding is applied in `agent`, `wallet`, and `payment` clients - Regression tests cover special-character ids for each client ## Suggested Label bug
opportunities.eligibilityReason: Payout evidence is below the bootstrap confidence threshold.

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $80] Raise a clear error for 200 responses with empty JSON bodies
opportunities.summary: ## Context `parseResponse` in `src/http/fetch-http-client.ts` (lines 148-160) calls `response.json()` whenever the `content-type` is `application/json`. When the server returns 200 with an empty body (common for some backends), `response.json()` throws a raw `SyntaxError`. In the request loop that error falls into the `catch` (line 70), is not an `AbortError` or `LilyApiError`, and for GET/PUT/DELETE it is silently retried and finally surfaced as `LilyTransportError` with code `TRANSPORT_ERROR` (lines 84-93) — a misleading diagnosis for what is really a payload mismatch. ## Proposed Change Catch empty-body JSON parse failures inside `parseResponse` and return `null` (mirroring the 204 path), or wrap the failure in a `LilyValidationError` with a message naming the status and content-type so callers can distinguish it from a network failure. ## Acceptance Criteria - A 200 with `content-type: application/json` and an empty body no longer throws `SyntaxError` - The failure is surfaced as a typed error, not a `TRANSPORT_ERROR` retry - A regression test covers the empty-JSON-body case ## Suggested Label bug
opportunities.eligibilityReason: Payout evidence is below the bootstrap confidence threshold.

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $80] Send `Idempotency-Key` header from `ExecutePaymentRequest.idempotencyKey`
opportunities.summary: ## Context `ExecutePaymentRequest` declares `idempotencyKey?: string` (`src/models/payment.ts`, line 32) and `PaymentClient.execute` forwards the whole body (`src/clients/payment-client.ts`, lines 19-25), but nothing in the transport (`src/http/fetch-http-client.ts`, `buildHeaders` lines 117-138) ever maps that field onto an `Idempotency-Key` header. The key is dead config: callers believe retry-safety is configured, but the backend never sees it and duplicate payment submissions are still possible. ## Proposed Change In `PaymentClient.execute`, lift `input.idempotencyKey` into `request.headers['Idempotency-Key']` (and keep it in the body if the backend expects it, pending contract confirmation). opportunities.title: [Bounty: $65] Reject empty-string `apiKey` and `authToken` during config resolution
opportunities.summary: ## Context `resolveLilySdkConfig` (`src/config/resolve-config.ts`, lines 42-43) copies credentials with `...(config.apiKey ? { apiKey } : {})`, so passing `apiKey: ''` or `authToken: ''` is silently dropped with no error. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
